Traditional Soft Pretzels

Served at: Martinstag Lantern Evening · Krampusnacht

Makes 10-12 pretzelsPrep 2 hours (includes rising time)Cook 12-15 min

These classic soft pretzels are a beloved treat, perfect for communal gatherings during the festive season. They make a wonderful, comforting snack for Martinstag Lantern Evening, offering a warm and savory bite after a lantern walk, and are equally fitting as a hearty accompaniment to the more whimsical treats of Krampusnacht.

Ingredients

  • 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) warm water (105-115°F / 40-46°C)
  • 1 tablespoon (10g) active dry yeast
  • 1 teaspoon (4g) granulated sugar
  • 4 1/2 cups (540g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons (9g) fine sea salt
  • 2 tablespoons (28g) unsalted butter, melted
  • 8 cups (1.9 liters) water (for boiling bath)
  • 1/2 cup (120g) baking soda (for boiling bath)
  • 1 large egg, beaten with 1 tablespoon water (for egg wash, optional)
  • 2 tablespoons (30g) coarse pretzel salt

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and granulated sugar. Stir gently and let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. In a separate large bowl, whisk together the flour and fine sea salt.
  3. Add the yeast mixture and melted butter to the flour mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
  4. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes, until it is smooth and elastic.
  5. Lightly grease a clean bowl with oil, place the dough in it, turning once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let rise in a warm place for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, or until doubled in size.
  6. While the dough rises, preheat your oven to 450°F (230°C). Line two large baking sheets with parchment paper.
  7. Once the dough has risen, gently punch it down. Divide the dough into 10-12 equal pieces.
  8. Roll each piece of dough into a long rope, about 20-24 inches (50-60 cm) long and 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) thick, tapering slightly at the ends.
  9. To shape a pretzel, form the rope into a U-shape. Cross the ends over each other twice, then bring them down and press them firmly onto the bottom curve of the U to secure.
  10. In a large pot, bring 8 cups (1.9 liters) of water to a rolling boil. Carefully add the 1/2 cup (120g) of baking soda. The mixture will foam up significantly.
  11. Working one or two at a time, carefully drop the shaped pretzels into the boiling baking soda solution. Boil for 20-30 seconds per side, then remove with a slotted spoon or spider and place them on the prepared baking sheets.
  12. If using, brush the tops of the pretzels with the egg wash. Generously sprinkle each pretzel with coarse pretzel salt.
  13. Using a sharp knife or razor blade, make a shallow cut (about 1/2 inch / 1.25 cm deep) across the thickest part of the bottom curve of each pretzel.
  14. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the pretzels are a deep golden brown. Transfer to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving.
  15. Serve warm.

Tips

  • For Martinstag, you can shape some dough into a 'Martinsgans' (goose) or a simple lantern shape before boiling and baking.
  • These pretzels are best enjoyed fresh and warm. Reheat leftover pretzels in a 350°F (175°C) oven for 5-7 minutes.
  • Serve with a variety of mustards (sweet, spicy, or Dijon), a warm cheese dip, or simply with butter for a truly traditional experience.
